content: Cefepime hydrochloride, marketed under the brand name MAXIPIME, is a semi-synthetic, broad-spectrum cephalosporin antibiotic designed for parenteral administration. Its chemical name is 1-[2-carboxy-8-oxo-5-thia-1-azabicyclo[4.2.0]oct-2-en-3-yl]methyl]-1-methylpyrrolidinium chloride, 72-(Z)-(O-methyloxime), monohydrochloride, monohydrate. The structural formula corresponds to this chemical composition. Cefepime hydrochloride appears as a white to pale yellow powder. It contains an equivalent of no less than 825 micrograms and no more than 911 micrograms of cefepime (C19H24N6O5S2) per milligram, calculated on an anhydrous basis. The compound is highly soluble in water. MAXIPIME for Injection is available for intramuscular or intravenous administration in strengths equivalent to 500 mg, 1 g, and 2 g of cefepime. It is supplied as a sterile, dry mixture of cefepime hydrochloride and L-arginine. The product contains no less than 90% and no more than 115% of the labeled amount of cefepime (C19H24N6O5S2). L-arginine is included at an approximate concentration of 707 mg per gram of cefepime to regulate the pH of the reconstituted solution, maintaining it between 4 and 6. When freshly reconstituted, MAXIPIME solutions range in color from pale yellow to amber.
